chunks: Hariz narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma), what is upon them from that which secures their blood and their wealth? He said: 'The land tax (Kharaj). If the poll tax (Jizyah) is taken from their heads, then there is no claim on their lands; and if the land tax is taken from their lands, then there is no claim on their heads.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Islamic rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between Jizyah and Kharaj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies the fiscal principle of exclusivity between the poll tax (Jizyah) and land tax (Kharaj), ensuring that the security of blood and property is not doubly taxed. It reflects the juristic consensus that Jizyah is a personal levy for individual protection, whereas Kharaj is a territorial levy on agricultural produce, thereby preventing financial burden on the Ahl al-Dhimma for the same right. This distinction underscores the pragmatic application of Islamic governance in managing diverse populations within the early Caliphate.
